scene_translation: The man walked without hesitation through the narrow alleys of Jinbocho, never once looking back — as though he had known from the very start that someone was following him. At last he stopped before a weathered iron door and slowly turned his face toward you. '...So you finally came. I've been waiting for you, Tesuto. Your grandmother told me that someday it would come to this.' His voice was low, carrying a certain weariness within it.
grammar_note: 【あたかも〜かのように】A literary simile meaning 'as if / as though.' あたかも＋clause＋かのように describes something that appears to be a certain way without actually being confirmed as such. It's more formal and literary than まるで〜みたいに. Note also the rough older-man register in 「待っていたぞ」— the sentence-final ぞ signals masculine, slightly gruff speech, contrasting with the more neutral politeness the player has encountered elsewhere.

mystery_memo: The grey-suited man (Relationship: cautiously neutral → now openly engaging) has confirmed he knew the player's deceased grandmother and was expecting this meeting. He is not hostile — he has been waiting. The iron door likely leads to the underground passages partially mapped in the notebook. The old shopkeeper's fear may stem from knowing this man or whoever he works for. The coin locker key and notebook are almost certainly relevant to what lies beyond the door. Key question now: what did the grandmother tell him, and what is the player's role in whatever was set in motion?
